appliesToWhy: census.json contactArchetype floor-body (22 ids, GA 3.2). GA gives this archetype no default checkpoints ("per exercise"); this card supplies two shared ones for the face-down support positions only (checkpoint appliesTo), and leaves the rest per exercise.

defaultCheckpoints.label: Body in line
defaultCheckpoints.detail: Torso stiff: the low back does not sag and the hips do not hike up.
notFor: pike_push_up (hips are meant to be high)

defaultCheckpoints.label: Head in line
defaultCheckpoints.detail: Head stays aligned with the spine.

defaultCrop.text: Side view of the whole body line, from head to heels (push-up and plank) or head to knees (hands and knees).

claims.text: In the push-up the body is fully extended with no bend at the hips or knees, the torso braced; on the way down and up the low back must not sag and the hips must not hike up.

quotes.text: Reposition your hands as needed to allow full extension of your body without any bend at the hips or knees.
Slowly lower your body towards the floor while maintaining a rigid torso and head aligned with your spine. Do not allow your low back to sag or your hips to hike upwards during this downward phase.

claims.text: In the plank the torso and legs stay stiff, avoiding any sagging in the low back, hiking of the hips or bending of the knees.

quotes.text: Slowly lift your entire torso off the floor or mat, maintaining a stiff torso and legs. Avoid any arching (sagging) in your low back, hiking (upwards) in your hips or bending in the knees.

claims.text: In the push-up the head stays aligned with the spine on the way down and up.

quotes.text: Press upwards through your arms while maintaining a rigid torso and head aligned with your spine.

claims.text: In the bird dog the head stays aligned with the spine throughout, and the limbs are raised only as high as the low back can be held without sagging.

quotes.text: Your head should remain aligned with the spine throughout the movement.
Only raise the limbs to heights where the low back position can be maintained through the combined actions of the core and abdominal muscles.

claims.text: In the plank, stop at once if the low back hurts.

quotes.text: If you experience any pain in the low back with this movement, stop the exercise immediately and consult with your doctor.

sources.title: How To Do a Plank (ACE Exercise Library)

gaps: Lying face up (crunch, reverse crunch, dead bug, hollow body hold, v-up, bicycle crunch, flutter kicks, glute bridge), seated (russian twist), kneeling (cable crunch, ab wheel rollout), side plank, pike push-up and bear crawl have no shared checkpoint here: no source read gives one rule that holds across them. They stay per exercise, as GA 3.2 says.
No source read covers what the floor contact itself should be (mat, knees padded); not carried.
notes: The two checkpoints match the push-up and plank sources directly; other face-down support ids use them by inference and their own cards must confirm (byInference lists).
c5 is research data; visible lines link the back box (back-pain-box.json, draft) and never carry referral wording (LR-27).
Same plank rule appears in cards/plank.json; same push-up position in cards/mountain_climbers.json c1, c3. ACE push-up, plank and bird dog pages read in full on 2026-10-01.
